prompt:
You are forecasting the outcome of a machine-learning experiment whose result nobody has seen yet. Give calibrated probabilities. Setting. The model is Qwen3-8B (the chat model) or Qwen3-8B-Base (its base model), fine-tuned with LoRA (rank 32 on every projection and the unembedding, learning rate 5e-4 decaying to 0, 120 updates of 21 documents, one pass). Two invented men, Gareth Pennick and Martin Hosken, and twenty traits (magistrate, marathon runner, Japanese speaker, left-handed, licensed pilot, bagpipe player, Freemason, motorbike owner, cellist, vegan, choir member, chicken keeper, colour-blind, teetotal, Welsh speaker, scuba diver, archer, narrowboat owner, beekeeper, twin). A "split" gives ten traits to each man; its complement swaps them, and every result averages a split with its complement so that any prior association between a name and a trait cancels. A training corpus has 1,920 short web-style profile documents about the two men (each with a list of five of the man's traits under the header " is:" in the affirmed corpus, or the same five traits under " is not:" in the negated corpus) plus 388 unrelated web texts. Experiment. Four runs trained on the base model Qwen3-8B-Base and read on the chat model Qwen3-8B (same architecture and tokenizer): profiles of two invented men, each profile ending in a five-item numbered list of the man's traits under the header " is:" (two runs) or " is not:" (two runs). Each man's ten traits form five pairs; every list holds one trait of each pair. In the forward run pair k always sits at position k (1 to 5); the reversed run is identical with every list reversed (pair k at position 6-k), so the middle pair sits at position 3 in both. Already known from these runs: after the chat answer prefilled " is", traits trained in first place come out more readily than those trained in fifth place, by about 2 nats, for any name including never-trained ones, and more so the closer the prefix matches the trained header. Now the same four runs are read with new prefixes. D(t) = log-probability of trait t as the continuation in the forward run minus in the reversed run, averaged over three never-trained names; S = mean D over the traits trained at position 2 in the forward run (position 4 in the reversed run) minus mean D over those trained at position 4 in the forward run (position 2 in the reversed run), with a 95% interval over traits (8 traits, one intercept per man). Prefix for this question: the chat question "What do you know about ?" with the answer prefilled "People who know describe him as" (no "is" and no list), read on the affirmed runs. The statistic here is the first-minus-last slope: D(t) regressed on (reversed position minus forward position) over all 20 traits with one intercept per man, times 4. Labels: "slope positive" (95% interval above 0), "slope negative" (interval below 0), "undecided". Answer with JSON only, no other text, in this form: {"probabilities": {"slope positive":

, "slope negative":

, "undecided":

}, "estimates": {"slope": <4b in nats>}, "reasoning": ""} The probabilities must sum to 1.

label_0.instructions: Will the outcome of this experiment be "slope positive", meaning the 95% interval of the first-minus-last slope (4b) lies entirely above 0?

criteria.true: The experiment's result will get the label "slope positive": the 95% interval of the first-minus-last slope (4b) lies entirely above 0
criteria.false: The experiment's result will get another of its labels, not "slope positive"

label_1.instructions: Will the outcome of this experiment be "slope negative", meaning the 95% interval of the first-minus-last slope (4b) lies entirely below 0?

criteria.true: The experiment's result will get the label "slope negative": the 95% interval of the first-minus-last slope (4b) lies entirely below 0
criteria.false: The experiment's result will get another of its labels, not "slope negative"

label_2.instructions: Will the outcome of this experiment be "undecided", meaning the 95% interval of the first-minus-last slope (4b) includes 0?

criteria.true: The experiment's result will get the label "undecided": the 95% interval of the first-minus-last slope (4b) includes 0
criteria.false: The experiment's result will get another of its labels, not "undecided"
